comments.author: cdirubbio
comments.body:
### Things are more clear now

1. every `minSyncPeriod` seconds, so 14 seconds in my cluster, [a burst update token is accumulated](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/v1.33.9/pkg/util/async/bounded_frequency_runner.go#L183).
```
		// allow burst updates in short succession
		qps := float32(time.Second) / float32(minInterval)
		bfr.limiter = flowcontrol.NewTokenBucketRateLimiterWithClock(qps, burstRuns, timer)
```
2. Since endpoints are large quantity, syncs take long period of time, 8.8s as example from log.
```
I0327 22:54:10.837283       1 proxier.go:809] "SyncProxyRules complete" ipFamily="IPv4" elapsed="8.810873765s"
```
3. In those first 8.8s, 8/14 from qps are accumulated.. and 6 seconds later at `22:54:16`, we reach 14/14 and thus KP can burst and run its bfr function (the iptables-restore).
----
TLDR Not a bug, just not something well documented it appears/misleading docs/code comments

comments.author: danwinship
comments.body:
Yeah, I think this is because of the "bursts", which no longer exists in the updated version of BoundedFrequencyRunner in 1.34 and later. In the new code, we explicitly wait `minInterval` between every run:

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/6c1cd99aef09161ddb07b8ade6c9564e9b9bfe27/pkg/proxy/runner/bounded_frequency_runner.go#L135-L141

title: [Failing Test] user namespaces kubeconfig tests [LinuxOnly] [Feature:UserNamespacesSupport] [Serial]  Kubelet crashes on restart when idsPerPod changes with existing userns pods on disk
security_topic: kubelet restart failure when user namespace pod cleanup is incomplete
qa_summary: Whether changing kubelet userNamespaces.idsPerPod can crash the kubelet on restart while old userns pod directories remain on disk, as described in Kubernetes PR 137930.

comments.author: kannon92
comments.body:
### Which jobs are failing?

`ci-node-crio-swap-serial`

### Which tests are failing?

```
[sig-node] user namespaces kubeconfig tests [LinuxOnly] [Feature:UserNamespacesSupport] [Serial] test config using userNamespaces.idsPerPod honors idsPerPod in userns pods
```

`k8s.io/kubernetes/test/e2e_node/user_namespaces_test.go:71`

### Since when has it been failing?

Observed in job run [2034607623600345088](https://gcsweb.k8s.io/gcs/kubernetes-ci-logs/logs/ci-node-crio-swap-serial/2034607623600345088/artifacts/e2-standard-2-fedora-coreos-43-20260301-3-1-gcp-x86-64-117cbc54/).

### Testgrid link

N/A

### Reason for failure (if possible)

> **Note:** The following analysis is AI-summarized from the linked CI logs and source code.

The kubelet fatally crashes during restart when `userNamespaces.idsPerPod` is changed and a pod created with the previous `idsPerPod` value still has its directory on disk.

**Failing log line** (from [kubelet.log](https://gcsweb.k8s.io/gcs/kubernetes-ci-logs/logs/ci-node-crio-swap-serial/2034607623600345088/artifacts/e2-standard-2-fedora-coreos-43-20260301-3-1-gcp-x86-64-117cbc54/kubelet.log)):
```
E0319 12:51:56.731779  8547 run.go:72] "command failed" err="failed to run Kubelet: failed to create kubelet:
  create user namespace manager: record pod mappings for existing pod \"5982517a-d29a-4eae-887d-773f1f8a0548\":
  wrong user namespace length 131072"
```

**Sequence of events:**

1. The test sets `userNamespaces.idsPerPod = 131072` (65536 × 2) and restarts the kubelet.
2. A pod with `hostUsers: false` is created. The kubelet allocates a user namespace mapping with `length = 131072` and persists it to the pod's `userns` file on disk.
3. The pod succeeds and the test deletes it.
4. The AfterEach restores the original kubelet config (default `idsPerPod = 65536`) and restarts the kubelet.
5. During initialization, `MakeUserNsManager()` scans existing pod directories on disk (`pkg/kubelet/userns/userns_manager.go:185-190`). It finds the not-yet-cleaned-up pod directory, reads its `userns` file (which has `length = 131072`), and calls `record()`.
6. `record()` (`pkg/kubelet/userns/userns_manager.go:242-243`) performs a strict equality check:
   ```go
   if length != m.userNsLength {
       return fmt.Errorf("wrong user namespace length %v", length)
   }
   ```
   This fails because `131072 != 65536`, and the error is fatal — the kubelet never starts.
7. The AfterEach times out after 120s waiting for the kubelet health check, and the test is marked as FAILED.

**Impact:** This also means that outside of tests, changing `idsPerPod` in a kubelet config and restarting the kubelet will crash the kubelet if any pods using the old value still have directories on disk. The strict check in `record()` does not account for pods that were created with a different `idsPerPod`.

### Additional context

- [Full CI job logs](https://gcsweb.k8s.io/gcs/kubernetes-ci-logs/logs/ci-node-crio-swap-serial/2034607623600345088/artifacts/e2-standard-2-fedora-coreos-43-20260301-3-1-gcp-x86-64-117cbc54/)
- [build-log.txt](https://gcsweb.k8s.io/gcs/kubernetes-ci-logs/logs/ci-node-crio-swap-serial/2034607623600345088/build-log.txt)

/kind failing-test
/sig node

comments.author: kannon92
comments.body:
Another instance of this failure observed in a different job:

- **Job:** `ci-node-crio-kubelet-serial`
- **Prow link:** https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-ci-logs/logs/ci-node-crio-kubelet-serial/2034369301338656768

cc @rata @AkihiroSuda — could you take a look? The root cause appears to be the strict equality check in `record()` at `pkg/kubelet/userns/userns_manager.go:242`, which makes it impossible for the kubelet to restart with a different `idsPerPod` if any pods created with the old value still have directories on disk.

title: EKS 1.34  DaemonSet Controller created a lot of pod during node deletion
security_topic: Graceful node shutdown causing DaemonSet pod recreation loop
qa_summary: The developer needed to know whether the repeated DaemonSet pod recreation during node shutdown was caused by Graceful Node Shutdown behavior and what configuration change fixes it, and the answer is anchored on the EKS NodeConfig kubelet shutdownGracePeriod and shutdownGracePeriodCriticalPods settings.

comments.author: tomahkvt
comments.body:
### What happened?

Hello,

Since upgrading our cluster to Kubernetes version 1.34, we have encountered destructive behavior in system components during node decommission (scale-down/termination). The issue manifests as an infinite pod recreation cycle, causing significant overhead on the API server.

Issue Description:
When a node initiates the shutdown sequence, the Kubelet correctly begins rejecting pod execution. However, high-level controllers (specifically the DaemonSet Controller) do not interpret this state as final and continuously attempt to reschedule pods back onto the same shutting-down node.

Observed Symptoms:

1)Massive Pod Rejections: Pods are terminated or rejected with the error: Pod was rejected: Pod was rejected as the node is shutting down.

2)Scheduler Loop: The scheduler assigns a pod to the node -> Kubelet rejects it -> The Controller detects the missing pod and triggers a new request -> The Scheduler picks the same node again.

3)Affected System Components (stuck in Pending):

istio-cni-node, ztunnel

aws-node, kube-proxy

ebs-csi-node, efs-csi-node, s3-csi-node

eks-node-monitoring-agent, eks-pod-identity-agent

4)ztunnel Flapping: We are observing a critical anomaly where a single ztunnel pod goes through the "Create-Reject-Delete" cycle hundreds of times during a single node's removal. This creates parasitic load on etcd, the kube-apiserver, and Istio control plane.

Technical Context:

K8s Version: 1.34

Feature involved: Graceful Node Shutdown. It appears there is a regression in how Node Taints and Lifecycle states are synchronized between the Kubelet and the Scheduler in v1.34.

Impact: System pods remain in Pending indefinitely while the node is dying, preventing clean cluster scaling.

We request your assistance with the following:

Confirm if this is a known regression in the v1.34 Node Lifecycle / DaemonSet logic.

Provide recommendations for NodeLifecycleController or GracefulNodeShutdown configurations to prevent the Scheduler from targeting nodes in a shutdown state.

Advise if there is a temporary patch or a specific Feature Gate to resolve this race condition.

Best regards,

### What did you expect to happen?

In EKS 1.33 we didn't have such problem with cretion of 300 daemon pod during node deletion.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Please try to delete node with daemon set pods ztunnel

comments.author: brianpursley
comments.body:
Not saying this isn't a bug, but it might not be a Kubernetes 1.34 regression.  It could have suddenly started happening due to this EKS AMI change:
https://github.com/awslabs/amazon-eks-ami/blob/2bed73dc4fafb502298fa67534dc53a030e56b21/nodeadm/internal/kubelet/config.go#L245-L252

It looks like the default is `0s`, so if EKS didn't set it previously, it could have been using the default:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/f1ccd2d8aae47ee36994ee4e92462f00a3f2146b/pkg/kubelet/apis/config/types.go#L457-L467

comments.author: tomahkvt
comments.body:
We found the root cause of the issue and identified how to fix it.

On a node running Kubernetes version v1.34.4-eks-f69f56f, there was no explicit shutdownGracePeriod or shutdownGracePeriodCriticalPods configuration in /etc/kubernetes/kubelet/config.json.

On the affected node, the following default values were present:

cat /etc/kubernetes/kubelet/config.json | grep shut

"shutdownGracePeriod": "2m30s",
"shutdownGracePeriodCriticalPods": "30s",

To fix this, we changed these values in the configuration:

apiVersion: node.eks.aws/v1alpha1
kind: NodeConfig
spec:
kubelet:
config:
shutdownGracePeriodCriticalPods: 0s
shutdownGracePeriod: 10s

After this change, DaemonSet pods are no longer being evicted with the status "Node is shutting down", and the scheduler no longer tries to run these pods on a shutting-down node.
@brianpursley Thank you a lot for your help.

comments.author: bart0sh
comments.body:
@pohly 
> to fix the flake we probably need to keep monitoring the component and restart when it fails, independently of the initial health/readiness check.

I don't think we need to, at least for now. Here is what I've found in the logs of the failed job:

API server reports its readiness first time at **04:16:03.839246**:
```
I0318 04:16:03.839246   54695 httplog.go:134] "HTTP" verb="GET" URI="/readyz" latency="717.69µs" userAgent="kube-apiserver/v1.35.2 (linux/amd64) kubernetes/fdc9d74" audit-ID="e7c2e7dc-c319-4571-92a6-f11ec7bc1450" srcIP="[::1]:39572" apf_pl="exempt" apf_fs="exempt" apf_iseats=1 apf_fseats=0 apf_additionalLatency="0s" apf_execution_time="242.914µs" resp=200
```

However, KCM reports an error and fails at **04:16:02.823244**, trying to create an API server client one second earlier than the API server is ready:

```
E0318 04:16:02.823244   54676 controllermanager.go:575] "Error initializing a controller" err="failed to create Kubernetes client for \"replicaset-controller\": serviceaccounts \"replicaset-controller\" is forbidden: User \"system:kube-controller-manager\" cannot get resource \"serviceaccounts\" in API group \"\" in the namespace \"kube-system\"" controller="replicaset-controller"
E0318 04:16:02.823295   54676 controllermanager.go:257] "Error building controllers" err="failed to create Kubernetes client for \"replicaset-controller\": serviceaccounts \"replicaset-controller\" is forbidden: User \"system:kube-controller-manager\" cannot get resource \"serviceaccounts\" in API group \"\" in the namespace \"kube-system\""
2026-03-18 04:16:02.880940807 +0000 UTC m=+939.327299475: terminated, result: exit status 1
```

So, my (hopefully educated) guess is that KCM fails because it tries to work with not yet ready API server. Properly querying /readyz endpoint for API server should fix the issue. At least it worth trying. Submitted [the fix](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/137958), PTAL.


@richabanker
@nojnhuh

> surprisingly KCM doesnt have a readyz endpoint today. Looks like this has been discussed before, [ref](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/118158) which proposes having /readyz return 200 after all informers are synced

Any chance to get [the latest, but still 3 years old /readyz implementation for KCM](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/134869) merged in near future?

comments.author: bart0sh
comments.body:
@pohly Even after implementing proper /redyz checks for API server, [the flake is still there](https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-ci-logs/pr-logs/pull/137958/pull-kubernetes-dra-integration/2036702676116312064).

After some investigation I think I found out why.
Unlike 1st (init) and 2nd (upgrade) test phases, 3rd phase (downgrade) modifies cluster components [in a reverse order](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/v1.36.0-beta.0/test/utils/localupcluster/localupcluster.go#L379). 

So, downgrade begins in this order:  _kube-proxy_, _kubelet_, _kube-scheduler_, **_kube-controller-manager_**, _kube-api-server_. When downgraded _kube-controller-manager_ starts, _kube-api-server_ from the previous phase is still running, but just up to the point when _kube_controller_manager_ replies with HTTP 200 OK code to the /health request from localupcluster. After that the _kube_api_server_ is killed and _kube_controller_manager_ fails the same way as before. It doesn't happen all the time though. Some time _kube_controller_manager_ is able to start before the api server restart, sometimes not, that's why the test is flaky.

I don't know why it's done this way, but as a result we ended up with this shaky setup. We expect other components to work with both versions of the api server, which is changing while other components are starting and communicating with it.

If we can use the original order, this wouldn't happen. I'd even propose to first stop the components in a reverse order and then start modified versions in the original order for both upgrade and downgrade phases to prevent component crashes when api-server suddenly disappears.
WDYT?

comments.author: pohly
comments.body:
The order follows the recommended upgrade/downgrade procedure in kubernetes: apiserver must always be newer or equal to the rest of the components. So on a downgrade, one first has to downgrade the components, then the apiserver.

However, we currently do not actually *operate* the cluster in the version-skew state. There's a TODO in the code that we could add this, but currently we don't. We always proceed to converting the entire cluster before we test again. So from that perspective we could do what you suggest.

But before we do that, why does kube-controller-manager not survive a restart of the apiserver? Shouldn't it be able to handle that? This part still looks like a deficiency in kube-controller-manager to me that is worth fixing.

comments.author: bart0sh
comments.body:
> But before we do that, why does kube-controller-manager not survive a restart of the apiserver? Shouldn't it be able to handle that?

I'm not sure about this as this scenario is not similar to rolling updates, which the skew policy applies to. In a rolling  downgrade scenario running and fully operational downgraded KCM should survive api server downgrade. This is not the case here. We have a starting, not fully operational KCM at the time of ongoing api server downgrade.

According to the logs KCM queries api-server /helthz just before the api server is killed:

Here is a quote from the api-server log:
```

2026-03-18 04:16:00.774847764 +0000 UTC m=+937.221206452: killed because command context was canceled: modifying the component
```

And then if fails to get serviceaccounts from a downgraded api server, as it's not healthy/running yet:
This is a quote from the KCM log:
`E0318 04:16:02.823244   54676 controllermanager.go:575] "Error initializing a controller" err="failed to create Kubernetes client for \"replicaset-controller\": serviceaccounts \"replicaset-controller\" is forbidden: User \"system:kube-controller-manager\" cannot get resource \"serviceaccounts\" in API group \"\" in the namespace \"kube-system\"" controller="replicaset-controller"`
This happens in the init KCM phase, when it builds controllers. I can look how this is done for other controllers and if retry would help, but let's not do it right now.

title: CVE-2026-3864: CSI Driver for NFS path traversal via subDir may delete unintended directories on the NFS server
security_topic: path traversal in NFS CSI subDir leading to unintended deletion
qa_summary: Whether CVE-2026-3864 in the Kubernetes CSI Driver for NFS lets path traversal in subDir delete unintended directories, with the answer anchored by the fixed version v4.13.1 and the official CVE feed issue.

comments.author: ritazh
comments.body:
**CVSS Rating:**  
[CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:H/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:H/A:H](https://www.first.org/cvss/calculator/3-1#CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:H/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:H/A:H) — **Medium (6.5)**

A vulnerability was discovered in the Kubernetes CSI Driver for NFS where the subDir parameter in volume identifiers was insufficiently validated. Attackers with the ability to create PersistentVolumes referencing the NFS CSI driver could craft volume identifiers containing path traversal sequences (../). During volume deletion or cleanup operations, the driver could operate on unintended directories outside the intended managed path within the NFS export.

This may lead to deletion or modification of directories on the NFS server.

### Am I vulnerable?

You may be vulnerable if:
You run the CSI Driver for NFS (nfs.csi.k8s.io)
Your cluster allows users to create PersistentVolumes referencing the NFS CSI driver
Your CSI driver version does not validate traversal sequences in the subDir field


#### Affected Versions
All versions of the CSI Driver for NFS prior to the v4.13.1 release containing the fix for traversal validation are affected.

### How do I mitigate this vulnerability?

This issue can be mitigated by:
Upgrading the CSI Driver for NFS to a patched version
Restricting PersistentVolume creation privileges to trusted administrators
Reviewing NFS exports to ensure only intended directories are writable by the driver

As a best practice, untrusted users should not be granted permission to create arbitrary PersistentVolumes referencing external storage drivers.


#### Fixed Versions

CSI Driver for NFS versions >= v4.13.1

### Detection

To determine if your cluster may be affected:
Inspect PersistentVolumes using the NFS CSI driver and review the volumeHandle field.
Look for traversal sequences such as: `../`
Review CSI controller logs for unexpected directory operations. e.g. “Removing subPath: /tmp/mount-uuid/legitimate/../../../exports/subdir”

If you find evidence that this vulnerability has been exploited, please contact security@kubernetes.io

#### Acknowledgements

This vulnerability was reported by Shaul Ben Hai, Senior Staff Security Researcher from SentinelOne.

The issue was fixed by the CSI Driver for NFS maintainers and the Kubernetes Security Response Committee. 

Andy Zhang @andyzhangx
Rita Zhang @ritazh

title: client-go/gentype: fake.go in production package disables Go linker dead code elimination (+52 MB binary bloat)
security_topic: binary bloat and dead-code-elimination regression from transitive reflect.MethodByName usage
qa_summary: Whether the binary-bloat issue is actionable in Kubernetes or already resolved, anchored on #137451 and the cited Go issue golang/go#25081.

comments.author: bryantbiggs
comments.body:
## Summary

The `k8s.io/client-go/gentype` package includes `fake.go` in the same Go package as production code (`type.go`). Because Go compiles all non-test `.go` files in a package together, `fake.go`'s import of `k8s.io/client-go/testing` is included in every binary that uses typed Kubernetes clients — even when no fake/test code is used.

This transitively pulls in `google.golang.org/protobuf/internal/descfmt` and `google.golang.org/protobuf/internal/impl`, which use `reflect.MethodByName` with non-constant arguments. When the Go linker detects `reflect.MethodByName` is reachable, it [conservatively disables dead code elimination](https://github.com/golang/go/issues/25081) for **all exported methods on all reachable types**. This causes massive binary bloat for any program that also imports packages with large method sets, like `aws-sdk-go-v2/service/ec2`.

## Impact

Adding a blank import of `k8s.io/client-go/gentype` to a program that uses the AWS EC2 SDK increases binary size by **+52 MB** (from 13 MB to 65 MB), linking 2,273 `ec2.Client` methods instead of the 7 actually needed.

This affects **every consumer of typed Kubernetes clients** (`kubernetes/typed/*/v*`), since they all import `gentype`.

## Root Cause

The import chain:

```
k8s.io/client-go/gentype (fake.go)
  └─ k8s.io/client-go/testing
       ├─ k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/util/managedfields
       └─ k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/util/strategicpatch
            └─ ... (several hops) ...
                 └─ google.golang.org/protobuf/internal/descfmt
                      └─ reflect.ValueOf(vs).MethodByName("Get")  [stringer.go:44, 99]
                 └─ google.golang.org/protobuf/internal/impl
                      └─ reflect.PtrTo(t).MethodByName(...)  [message.go:198, 201]
```

The Go linker sees `reflect.MethodByName` is reachable and disables method pruning globally. See [golang/go#25081](https://github.com/golang/go/issues/25081) and [kubernetes/kubernetes#132216](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/132216) for background.

## Reproduction

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
DIR=$(mktemp -d)
trap "rm -rf $DIR" EXIT
cd "$DIR"

go mod init gentype-dce-repro

cat > baseline.go << 'GOEOF'
//go:build baseline
package main

import (
    "context"
    "fmt"
    "github.com/aws/aws-sdk-go-v2/config"
    "github.com/aws/aws-sdk-go-v2/service/ec2"
)

type EC2API interface {
    DescribeInstances(ctx context.Context, params *ec2.DescribeInstancesInput, optFns ...func(*ec2.Options)) (*ec2.DescribeInstancesOutput, error)
}

func main() {
    cfg, _ := config.LoadDefaultConfig(context.Background())
    var client EC2API = ec2.NewFromConfig(cfg)
    out, _ := client.DescribeInstances(context.Background(), &ec2.DescribeInstancesInput{InstanceIds: []string{"i-test"}})
    fmt.Println(out)
}
GOEOF

cat > with_gentype.go << 'GOEOF'
//go:build with_gentype
package main

import (
    "context"
    "fmt"
    "github.com/aws/aws-sdk-go-v2/config"
    "github.com/aws/aws-sdk-go-v2/service/ec2"
    _ "k8s.io/client-go/gentype"
)

type EC2API interface {
    DescribeInstances(ctx context.Context, params *ec2.DescribeInstancesInput, optFns ...func(*ec2.Options)) (*ec2.DescribeInstancesOutput, error)
}

func main() {
    cfg, _ := config.LoadDefaultConfig(context.Background())
    var client EC2API = ec2.NewFromConfig(cfg)
    out, _ := client.DescribeInstances(context.Background(), &ec2.DescribeInstancesInput{InstanceIds: []string{"i-test"}})
    fmt.Println(out)
}
GOEOF

go mod tidy

echo "=== Go version ==="
go version

echo ""
echo "=== Baseline (EC2 SDK only) ==="
go build -tags baseline -o bin_baseline .
echo "Size: $(stat --format=%s bin_baseline) bytes ($(du -h bin_baseline | cut -f1))"
echo "ec2.Client methods linked: $(go tool nm bin_baseline | grep -c 'service/ec2\.(\*Client)\.')"

echo ""
echo "=== With gentype (blank import) ==="
go build -tags with_gentype -o bin_gentype .
echo "Size: $(stat --format=%s bin_gentype) bytes ($(du -h bin_gentype | cut -f1))"
echo "ec2.Client methods linked: $(go tool nm bin_gentype | grep -c 'service/ec2\.(\*Client)\.')"
```

### Results (Go 1.26.1 linux/amd64, client-go v0.35.2, ec2 v1.294.1)

| Build | Binary Size | `ec2.Client` methods linked |
|---|---|---|
| Baseline (EC2 SDK only) | 13 MB | 7 (just `DescribeInstances` + helpers) |
| + `k8s.io/client-go/gentype` (blank import) | 65 MB | 2,273 (all EC2 API operations) |
| **Difference** | **+52 MB** | **+2,266 dead methods** |

## Suggested Fix

Move `fake.go` out of the `gentype` package so that test fake infrastructure is not compiled into production binaries. Options:

1. **Move to a subpackage**: `k8s.io/client-go/gentype/fake` (analogous to how `k8s.io/client-go/kubernetes/fake` is separate from `k8s.io/client-go/kubernetes`)
2. **Use a build tag**: Add a build constraint to `fake.go` to exclude it from production builds

Either approach would break the `gentype -> testing -> protobuf -> reflect.MethodByName` chain for production builds, allowing the Go linker to properly eliminate dead code.

## Related Issues

- [golang/go#25081](https://github.com/golang/go/issues/25081) — Enable linker dead code pruning when using reflect
- [golang/go#60221](https://github.com/golang/go/issues/60221) — There should be a way to determine why deadcode elimination was not performed
- [kubernetes/kubernetes#132216](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/132216) — Allow linker to perform dead code elimination for kube-apiserver etc
- [kubernetes/kubernetes#127888](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/127888) — Make client-go lighter and easier to consume (Umbrella)

/kind bug
/sig api-machinery

comments.author: bryantbiggs
comments.body:
## Update: Root cause traced to protobuf Go 1.26 regression

Further investigation reveals the root cause is a **Go 1.26-specific regression** in `google.golang.org/protobuf`, not specific to gentype's `fake.go`.

### What's happening

Go 1.26 added `reflect.Value.Methods()`. Protobuf's `internal/descfmt/stringer.go` calls `MethodByName("Methods")`, which now matches this new stdlib method. This causes the Go linker to retain `reflect.Value.Methods()`, which in turn **disables dead code elimination globally** for all exported methods on all reachable types.

This affects **any Go 1.26 binary** that transitively imports `google.golang.org/protobuf` — not just through gentype, but also through:
- `k8s.io/client-go/discovery` → gnostic-models → protobuf
- `github.com/prometheus/client_golang` → client_model → protobuf
- Any other protobuf consumer

### Already fixed upstream (unreleased)

The protobuf team has already fixed this on master in two commits, but **neither is in any released version** (latest is v1.36.11):

- [golang/protobuf#1704](https://github.com/golang/protobuf/issues/1704) — Fix for `MethodByName("Methods")` conflicting with Go 1.26's `reflect.Value.Methods()` (commit `cb6ac5a2`, Jan 2026)
- [golang/protobuf#1708](https://github.com/golang/protobuf/issues/1708) — Replace all remaining `MethodByName` calls with direct interface casts (commit `8c4c4ae4`, Jan 2026)

### Impact on this issue

The gentype `fake.go` issue is still valid — it adds an unnecessary import chain (`gentype → testing → managedfields → protobuf`) that wouldn't exist if fakes were in a subpackage. However, **for Go 1.26 builds, the binary bloat will occur through any protobuf import path**, not just gentype.

Once `google.golang.org/protobuf` releases a version containing these fixes, the DCE regression should be resolved for all Go 1.26 consumers. Until then, any Kubernetes consumer building with Go 1.26 is affected.

### Related issues

- [golang/protobuf#1561](https://github.com/golang/protobuf/issues/1561) — Original MethodByName optimization (fixed in v1.32.0)
- [golang/protobuf#1704](https://github.com/golang/protobuf/issues/1704) — Go 1.26 regression fix (merged, unreleased)
- [golang/protobuf#1708](https://github.com/golang/protobuf/issues/1708) — Full MethodByName removal follow-up (merged, unreleased)
- [golang/go#62257](https://github.com/golang/go/issues/62257) — Go 1.22 linker improvement for constant-string MethodByName

comments.author: bryantbiggs
comments.body:
Closing this issue — after deeper investigation, this is not actionable for the Kubernetes project.

## What we found

The initial analysis correctly identified that `gentype/fake.go` introduces an unnecessary import chain to `protobuf/internal/descfmt` (which uses `reflect.MethodByName`). However, further investigation revealed:

1. **K8s already addressed the protobuf regression** in #137451 (pinning protobuf to a commit with the Go 1.26 DCE fix). This resolves the issue for K8s server binaries.

2. **For projects using Cobra** (like ours — aws-iam-authenticator), the Go linker's dead code elimination is disabled regardless of protobuf, because `text/template/exec.go` uses `reflect.Value.MethodByName(fieldName)` with a **runtime variable** argument. Since Cobra imports `text/template` for help/usage rendering, ALL exported methods on ALL reachable types are retained no matter what. The gentype/protobuf path is redundant.

3. **The root cause is in the Go stdlib** (`text/template`), tracked at [golang/go#25081](https://github.com/golang/go/issues/25081). This is not something the Kubernetes project can fix.

While moving `fake.go` to a subpackage would be good hygiene (avoiding unnecessary test infrastructure in production builds), it would not produce measurable binary size improvements for any real-world consumer, since other import paths (Prometheus, K8s discovery, or `text/template` via Cobra) already trigger the same linker behavior.

Apologies for the noise.

comments.author: kannon92
comments.body:
> **Note:** This analysis was generated by AI (Claude) and should be verified by a human reviewer.

**Edit:** Updated with the correct date range — the original analysis used the wrong year for git log queries.

## Analysis of Failing Static Pod Test

### What the test does

The test at `test/e2e_node/static_pod_test.go:106` creates a static pod with an init container, waits for the init container to complete and records `pod.Status.StartTime`, then removes the init container and restarts kubelet. It expects the mirror pod to get a **new `StartTime`** after restart (indicating the pod was recreated). The failure shows both timestamps are identical — the pod is not being recreated as expected.

### Recent commits that could impact this (Mar 7–14, 2026)

#### 1. PR #137362 — `on-demand-relist` (@tallclair)
- Major changes to PLEG (`pleg/generic.go`, +270 lines), `pod_workers.go`, `kubelet.go`, and pod cache
- Introduces on-demand PLEG pod relisting, per-pod cache refresh timestamps, and changes to sync result handling
- Modifies how pod workers request relisting, which directly affects pod lifecycle detection after kubelet restart

#### 2. PR #137566 — `fixgetpods` (@yangjunmyfm192085)
- Changes container sorting in `kubeGenericRuntimeManager.GetPods()` and `GetPod()` to sort by create time and ID
- Merged March 13 — the same day the failures started
- Could affect which container state is returned for static pods after kubelet restart

#### 3. PR #134768 — `pod-level-resource-managers` (@KevinTMtz)
- Pod-level CPU & Memory managers support, topology manager support, pod-level state
- Touches `kubelet.go` and resource manager integration

#### 4. PR #136681 — `restart-pod` (@yuanwang04)
- Graduates `RestartAllContainers` feature to beta (now enabled by default)
- Also includes `cf33d3ace34` — "Fix LastTerminationStatus for RestartAllContainers" which modifies `kubelet_pods.go`
- A newly-default-enabled feature affecting container restart behavior could change how static pods behave after kubelet restart

#### 5. PR #137248 — `propagate-context-cri-client` (@SergeyKanzhelev)
- Propagates context to CRI client `Close` and uses contextual logging

#### 6. PR #136185 — `ndf-bitmap` (@tallclair)
- Switches `NodeDeclaredFeatures` to bitmapped FeatureSet implementation, adds global default NDF registry

cc @tallclair @yangjunmyfm192085 @KevinTMtz @yuanwang04 @SergeyKanzhelev — could you take a look and see if any of these changes might be related to the static pod test failures?

comments.author: tallclair
comments.body:
I honestly can't figure out what this test is trying to verify with the StartTime check.

The StartTime is set by the status manager, and the status manager tries to preserve StartTime so it doesn't change:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/76a3d535a18a68ca63e12e05e8bd93a14eef90c0/pkg/kubelet/status/status_manager.go#L836

To get the oldStatus, it first check's it's cache, then tries to fetch the mirror pod:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/76a3d535a18a68ca63e12e05e8bd93a14eef90c0/pkg/kubelet/status/status_manager.go#L793-L806

After the Kubelet restarts, the status cache should initially be empty, so whether the StartTime is preserved will depend on whether the Kubelet has injested the MirrorPod into the pod manager yet. This is inherently racy, and I don't know why the test is expecting the StartTime change in the first place...

comments.author: tallclair
comments.body:
OK, I think the test flakiness was triggered by the delayed startup that was accidentally introduced with the on-demand pleg changes. Since the PLEG waited the full 1s relist period, it meant there was a delay to first sync, so the kubelet was much more likely to have already added the mirror pod to its cache. The delay was fixed by https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/137778, which merged 2 days ago, correlating to the drop off of this test.

We should still change the test, since the check doesn't make sense (and there were a few flakes before the on-demand changes merged), but the increased flakiness is essentially fixed.

comments.author: dgrisonnet
comments.body:
The issue seems to be caused by https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/137471 which was merged on the day we started seeing the failures: https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-ci-logs/logs/ci-kubernetes-kubemark-100-gce/2030165951168647168

I wrote a quick unit test and I am seeing the following race:
 1. Pod has sandbox A (READY). PLEG Relist calls GetPods(), taking a snapshot
   at time T1 that includes sandbox A.                                        
  2. Sandbox A becomes NOT_READY. SyncPod detects this with a fresh status and
   creates sandbox B (READY). This happens between T1 and when PLEG processes 
  this pod.
  3. PLEG's reconcilePodRecord calls updateCache -> GetPodStatus(ctx, pod) with
   the stale T1 snapshot. Because GetPodStatus now iterates pod.Sandboxes     
  instead of querying the CRI, it only sees sandbox A (NOT_READY) and misses
  sandbox B entirely.                                                         
  4. The pod worker reads this stale cached status. PodSandboxChanged sees no
  READY sandbox and triggers SyncPod. killPodWithSyncResult kills sandbox A   
  (the only one in the stale status) but does not kill sandbox B (invisible).
  SyncPod then creates sandbox C (READY).                                     
  5. The runtime now has two READY sandboxes for the same pod: B and C.

This situation will be corrected by https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/1ed5965382e09c1fdc8b363c153e9ebee0942481/pkg/kubelet/kuberuntime/util/util.go#L45-L50 but in the meantime, kubelet will try to create metrics from two different sandboxes for the same pod which is causing the duplication issue on `kubelet_container_log_filesystem_used_bytes`.

@tallclair is this an expected behavior?

comments.author: tallclair
comments.body:
@dgrisonnet I'll need to dig into the code for this, but I'm confused by step 2 in your breakdown

> Sandbox A becomes NOT_READY. SyncPod detects this with a fresh status and
creates sandbox B (READY). This happens between T1 and when PLEG processes
this pod.

`SyncPod` should only ever operate on the results of the PLEG relist:

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/1ed5965382e09c1fdc8b363c153e9ebee0942481/pkg/kubelet/pod_workers.go#L1266-L1274

So for SyncPod to see the NOT_READY Sandbox A, the PLEG would have had to do a Relist that read the NOT_READY sandbox A. Unless I'm missing something, I don't think SyncPod can see a NOT_READY sandbox A while the pleg is still operating on a READY sandbox A.

That said, I think there's a different race condition:

1. SyncPod is running at time T0
2. PLEG global Relist starts at time T1, and reads the pod sandboxes, with none ready
3. SyncPod, still running, starts a new sandbox, Sandbox B, and finishes running (lastSyncTime=T2)
4. PLEG relist calls update status for the pod, but doesn't know about Sandbox B. It writes the cache update at time T3
5. SyncPod runs again, calls GetNewerThan with last sync time T2, and gets the pod status from step 4, since T3 > T2. However, this status is missing Sandbox B.
6. SyncPod starts a new Sandbox C

I think the issue is that the timestamp used in step 4 is _after_ the time of the relist. As long as we use the T1 timestamp in step 4, it shouldn't be a problem. I'll send a PR.

You are correct, I looked at the code again and that's not possible. I was under the impression that it had to do with the statuses and missed the issue with the timestamps.

Hey guys,

Could you please clarify [CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H](https://www.first.org/cvss/calculator/3.1#CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H) ? If I understood correctly, to exploit this vulnerability attacker should be authenticated to Kubernetes cluster and have role with permissions to modify ingress objects.

Is it correct? If so, does it mean that attack vector (AV) should be Local and Privileges Required (PR) is High.

Thank you in advanced.

CC: @tabbysable

comments.author: tabbysable
comments.body:
@omelnyk1 You are correct about the scope and impact of the vuln: it is a privilege escalation from "user with permission to create an ingress" to "probably cluster admin, depending on how the cluster is configured".

The difficulty you see is a constant tension with CVSS and software like Kubernetes. CVSS is best aligned with the security needs of desktop software, where there is a clear distinction between an attacker sitting at the keyboard and an attacker who is somewhere else. You will rarely see "local" attack vector in Kubernetes CVEs because local means someone who has an account on the server where the Kubernetes component is running--usually a control plane node. In the Kubernetes security model, it is discouraged and exceptionally rare for anyone other than trusted admins to have *any* access to that layer.

Similarly, in this CVE, "permissions required" is evaluated from the point of view of a cluster administrator who operates a cluster for use by engineers who run workloads on the cluster. So in this case, "none" would mean for example customers, "low" the engineers who run workloads but don't administer the cluster, and "high" the cluster administrators themselves. (This is also why you don't see many Kubernetes CVEs with high required privileges: there are not very many things that require cluster admin access and count as security vulnerabilities. Often, if a behavior is only available to cluster administrators, it's considered an ordinary bug or a dangerous feature.)

For more context on how the Security Response Committee considers these types of questions, see [our documentation on the subject](https://github.com/kubernetes/committee-security-response/blob/main/severity-ratings.md).

title: kube-apiserver removes all managedFields if conversion webhook is not available
security_topic: managedFields loss when conversion webhook is unavailable
qa_summary: Whether kube-apiserver’s managedFields loss on conversion-webhook failure is a bug and what code path preserves the existing fields, anchored on the linked fieldmanager.go source and the proposed patch in comment c3.

comments.author: sbueringer
comments.body:
### What happened?

The apiserver removes all managedFields of an object under the following circumstances:
* object has managedField entries of multiple apiVersions
* conversion webhook is (potentially temporarily) not available/reachable
* there's a write on the object (via label, or client-side apply, SSA just returns an appropriate error, more details below)

### What did you expect to happen?

I would expect to get an error back from the apiserver in cases like this.
Removing all managedFields can have a big impact on the results of subsequent writes.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Required files:
[cr_cluster.yaml](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/25218546/cr_cluster.yaml)
[cr_cluster_ssa.yaml](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/25218545/cr_cluster_ssa.yaml)
[crd_cluster.yaml](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/25218548/crd_cluster.yaml)
[crd_cluster_no_conversion.yaml](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/25218547/crd_cluster_no_conversion.yaml)

```bash
kind create cluster
```

Deploy the CRD (without conversion configured for now so we are able to prepare managedFields with v1beta1 & v1beta2)
```bash
kubectl apply -f ./crd_cluster_no_conversion.yaml
```

Deploy and prepare the cluster
```bash
kubectl apply -f ./cr_cluster.yaml
kubectl label clusters.v1beta1.cluster.x-k8s.io cluster-1  def=ghi --overwrite
kubectl label clusters.v1beta2.cluster.x-k8s.io cluster-1  abc=def --overwrite
kubectl get cluster cluster-1 -o json --show-managed-fields | jq '.metadata.managedFields' | grep apiVersion

kubectl apply -f ./crd_cluster.yaml

title: Some crashed or OOMKilled containers fail to restart in v1.35
security_topic: container restart failure after kubelet restart
qa_summary: Whether the kubelet restart-related container restart bug in v1.35 is fixed by the referenced commit 237996ca0ec076c5a149c7341d434b680c695720 and needs cherry-picking back to 1.35.

comments.author: DTLP
comments.body:
### What happened?

After upgrading Kubernetes from v1.34.2 to v1.35.0, we observed a scenario where a pod with multiple containers does not restart a crashed application container, leaving the pod in an Error state indefinitely.

This behavior was not observed on v1.34.2. Reverting the kubelet back to v1.34.2 causes the issue to disappear.

**Observed Behavior:**
The main container terminates but never restarts:
```
State:          Terminated
  Reason:       Error
  Exit Code:    2
  Started:      Tue, 27 Jan 2026 16:11:01 +0000
  Finished:     Tue, 10 Feb 2026 11:08:55 +0000
Ready:          False
Restart Count:  0
```

The sidecar container continues to run normally:
```
State:          Running
Started:        Tue, 27 Jan 2026 16:10:54 +0000
Ready:          True
Restart Count:  0
```

Pod conditions show:
```
Conditions:
  Type                        Status
  PodReadyToStartContainers   True
  Initialized                 True
  Ready                       False
  ContainersReady             False
  PodScheduled                True
```

No useful logs or errors appear in `kubectl describe pod` output, events, or `kubelet` logs.

**Notes:**
- This issue seems to only affect pods with more than one container
- We are unsure whether it's just pods with an `initContainer` or does it also apply to `container` sidecars
- Manually killing the process in the sidecar container or deleting the pod helps getting it back to working state
- `RestartAllContainersOnContainerExits` is not enabled

**Possibly related?**
- https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/134345

### What did you expect to happen?

Containers should reliably restart every time they crash.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

The best way we found to reproduce this is by running a pod with 2 containers: an initContainer with `restartPolicy: Always` and an application container that we manually crash with `kill 1` command.
It might not work right first time, but we managed to reproduce this multiple times getting pods stuck in Error state that they never recover from automatically.

### Anything else we need to know?

_No response_

title: kubelet nodeinfomanager does not reconcile CSINode ownerReference when Node is replaced with same name but different UID, leading to GC deletion
security_topic: CSINode ownerReference stale-UID garbage-collection bug
qa_summary: Whether the CSINode ownerReference UID mismatch bug is already fixed in Kubernetes, based on pull request https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/131098 and the note that it is fixed in v1.35 but not backported.

comments.author: rajeeshckr
comments.body:
### What happened? In our cluster, the node with same name got recreated, hence it should have the CSINode already there. notice kubelet start at `16:23:07.906` But, the GC collection of the CSINode happened after the new node was launched notice GC at `16:24:03.591`, that was done for instance ID `i-019f660891131cc51` When the kubelet on the new node started up, it failed to do any updates on CSINode making it eligible for GC shown above ### What did you expect to happen? When kubelet registers a CSI driver via tryUpdateCSINode in nodeinfomanager.go, and a CSINode object already exists for the node, kubelet should verify that the existing CSINode's ownerReference UID matches the current Node object's UID. If the UIDs do not match (e.g., the Node was replaced with the same name but a new UID), kubelet should either: * Delete the stale CSINode and recreate it with the correct ownerReference, or * Update the existing CSINode's ownerReference to reflect the current Node UID This would prevent the garbage collector from deleting a CSINode that was just successfully updated with valid driver registration info, simply because it still carried a stale ownerReference pointing to a previous Node UID that no longer exists. This is the same class of bug that was identified and fixed for Lease objects in #109777. ### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)? This is a race condition that depends on GC timing relative to CSI driver registration. In the normal case, GC deletes the stale CSINode before the new kubelet's CSI driver registers, so tryUpdateCSINode takes the CreateCSINode() path and everything works. The bug manifests when GC is delayed. Theoretical steps to reproduce: ``` # 1. Identify your node name NODE_NAME=$(kubectl get nodes -o jsonpath='{.items[0].metadata.name}') # 2. Record the current Node UID and CSINode ownerReference UID (should match) echo "Node UID: $(kubectl get node $NODE_NAME -o jsonpath='{.metadata.uid}')" echo "CSINode ref: $(kubectl get csinode $NODE_NAME -o jsonpath='{.metadata.ownerReferences[0].uid}')" # 3. Delete the Node object (kubelet will re-register it automatically with a new UID) kubectl delete node $NODE_NAME # 4. Wait for the node to re-register kubectl wait --for=condition=Ready node/$NODE_NAME --timeout=120s # 5. Compare UIDs again — they will NOT match echo "New Node UID: $(kubectl get node $NODE_NAME -o jsonpath='{.metadata.uid}')" echo "CSINode ownerRef UID: $(kubectl get csinode $NODE_NAME -o jsonpath='{.metadata.ownerReferences[0].uid}')" # 6. Wait for garbage collector to delete the stale CSINode (~30-60 seconds) echo "Waiting for GC to delete CSINode..." while kubectl get csinode $NODE_NAME &>/dev/null; do sleep 5 echo "CSINode still exists, waiting..." done echo "CSINode deleted by garbage collector" # 7. Confirm CSINode is gone and does not come back sleep 30 kubectl get csinode $NODE_NAME # Expected: Error from server (NotFound): csinodes.storage.k8s.io "" not found # 8. Create a PVC and pod to demonstrate the impact kubectl apply -f - <<'EOF' apiVersion: v1 kind: PersistentVolumeClaim metadata: name: csinode-repro-pvc spec: accessModes: - ReadWriteOnce resources: requests: storage: 1Gi --- apiVersion: v1 kind: Pod metadata: name: csinode-repro-pod spec: nodeName: NODE_NAME_PLACEHOLDER containers: - name: app image: busybox command: ["sleep", "3600"] volumeMounts: - name: data mountPath: /data volumes: - name: data persistentVolumeClaim: claimName: csinode-repro-pvc EOF # Patch in the actual node name kubectl patch pod csinode-repro-pod --type=json \ -p="[{\"op\":\"replace\",\"path\":\"/spec/nodeName\",\"value\":\"$NODE_NAME\"}]" 2>/dev/null || true # 9. Observe the volume attachment failure kubectl describe pod csinode-repro-pod | grep -A5 "Events" # Expected: # Warning FailedAttachVolume attachdetach-controller # AttachVolume.Attach failed for volume "pvc-xxx" : # csinode.storage.k8s.io "" not found # 10. Cleanup kubectl delete pod csinode-repro-pod --force --grace-period=0 2>/dev/null kubectl delete pvc csinode-repro-pvc 2>/dev/null ``` ### Anything else we need to know? _No response_ ### Kubernetes version
```console $ kubectl version "Kubelet version" kubeletVersion="v1.33.4" ```

AWS

title: Unable to verify cosign signature for kubectl 1.35.0 on amd64
security_topic: cosign signature verification failure for a release artifact

comments.author: nicholasdille
comments.body:
### What happened?

After downloading kubectl 1.35.0, I attempted to verify the cosign keyless signature. This failed for amd64 but succeeds for arm64.

I used the following command:

```bash
# amd64
cosign verify-blob https://dl.k8s.io/release/v1.35.0/bin/linux/amd64/kubectl \
    --signature https://dl.k8s.io/release/v1.35.0/bin/linux/amd64/kubectl.sig \
    --certificate https://dl.k8s.io/release/v1.35.0/bin/linux/amd64/kubectl.cert \
    --certificate-oidc-issuer https://accounts.google.com \
    --certificate-identity krel-staging@k8s-releng-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com

# arm64
cosign verify-blob https://dl.k8s.io/release/v1.35.0/bin/linux/arm64/kubectl \
    --signature https://dl.k8s.io/release/v1.35.0/bin/linux/arm64/kubectl.sig \
    --certificate https://dl.k8s.io/release/v1.35.0/bin/linux/arm64/kubectl.cert \
    --certificate-oidc-issuer https://accounts.google.com \
    --certificate-identity krel-staging@k8s-releng-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com
```

```

title: DRA: Scheduler CEL evaluation fails with "no such key" when accessing nested attributes without existence check
security_topic: CEL selector behavior for missing nested attributes
qa_summary: Whether CEL selectors for DRA should treat missing nested device attributes as false rather than a runtime error, and the answer is anchored in the Kubernetes API docs and CEL OptionalTypes documentation referenced by the maintainer.

comments.author: omeryahud
comments.body:
### What happened?

I am using DRA with a CEL selector to filter devices based on driver attributes. When writing an expression that accesses a nested field within `device.attributes`, the scheduler encounters a CEL runtime error if the specific driver key does not exist on the device, rather than evaluating the expression to false.

The following expression fails during the DynamicResources filter plugin execution:

```
cel:
  expression: 'device.attributes["gpu.nvidia.com"].sharingStrategy == "runai-fractions"'
```

### What did you expect to happen?

I expected the expression to evaluate to false for devices that do not possess the gpu.nvidia.com attribute, allowing the scheduler to simply skip those devices.

Instead, the scheduler treats this as a hard runtime error, preventing the claim from being allocated even if valid devices exist, or logging significant errors during the filter phase.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

```
apiVersion: resource.k8s.io/v1
kind: DeviceClass
metadata:
  name: gpu.nvidia.com
spec:
  selectors:
  - cel: 
      expression: "device.driver == 'gpu.nvidia.com'"
---
apiVersion: resource.k8s.io/v1
kind: ResourceSlice
metadata:
  name: kind-control-plane-gpu-devices-slice
spec:
  nodeName: kind-control-plane
  driver: gpu.nvidia.com

  pool:
    generation: 1
    resourceSliceCount: 1
    name: kind-control-plane-gpu-pool

  devices:
  - name: gpu-0
    bindsToNode: true

  - name: gpu-1
    attributes:
      sharingStrategy:
        string: runai-fractions
    bindsToNode: true
---
apiVersion: resource.k8s.io/v1
kind: ResourceClaim
metadata:
  name: kind-control-plane-gpu-runai-fractionable-claim-1
spec:
  devices:
    requests:
    - name: gpu-runai-fractionable
      exactly:
        deviceClassName: gpu.nvidia.com
        capacity:
          requests:
            memory: 10Gi
        selectors:
        - cel:
            expression: 'device.attributes["gpu.nvidia.com"].sharingStrategy == "runai-fractions"'
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: fraction-pod-1
spec:
  resourceClaims:
  - name: fraction-claim
    resourceClaimName: kind-control-plane-gpu-runai-fractionable-claim-1
  containers:
  - name: fraction-container
    resources:
      claims:
      - name: fraction-claim
    image: ubuntu:latest
    command: [ "/bin/bash", "-c", "--" ]
    args: [sleep Infinity"]
```

```
> kubectl describe pod fraction-pod-1
...
Events:
  Type     Reason            Age              From               Message
  ----     ------            ----             ----               -------
  Warning  FailedScheduling  3s               default-scheduler  0/1 nodes are available: 1 cannot allocate all claims. still not schedulable, preemption: 0/1 nodes are available: 1 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.
  Warning  FailedScheduling  1s (x2 over 3s)  default-scheduler  running "DynamicResources" filter plugin: claim default/kind-control-plane-gpu-runai-fractionable-claim-1: selector #0: CEL runtime error: no such key: sharingStrategy
```


### Anything else we need to know?

title: CVE-2025-13281: Portworx Half-Blind SSRF in kube-controller-manager
security_topic: mitigation and fixed versions for Portworx SSRF in kube-controller-manager
qa_summary: Whether CVE-2025-13281 in kube-controller-manager is fixed and what versions/PRs closed the half-blind SSRF in the in-tree Portworx StorageClass, anchored on the listed fixed versions and PRs #135081/#135193/#135192/#135191.

comments.author: natherz97
comments.body:
CVSS Rating: [CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:H/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:N/A:N](https://www.first.org/cvss/calculator/3-1#CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:H/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:N/A:N) - Medium (5.8)

A half-blind Server Side Request Forgery (SSRF) vulnerability exists in kube-controller-manager when using the in-tree Portworx StorageClass. This was patched for other in-tree StorageClasses (GlusterFS, Quobyte, StorageOS, and ScaleIO) as part of[ CVE-2020-8555](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/91542). This vulnerability allows authorized users to leak arbitrary information from unprotected endpoints in the control plane’s host network (including link-local or loopback services). 

An attacker with permissions to create a pod using the built-in Portworx StorageClass can cause kube-controller-manager to make GET requests (without an attacker controlled request body) from within the control plane’s host network and make the corresponding HTTP response body visible as part of event objects created by kube-controller-manager.

The in-tree Portworx StorageClass has been disabled by default starting in version v1.31 from the CSIMigrationPortworx feature gate. As a result, currently supported versions greater than or equal to v1.32 are not impacted unless the CSIMigrationPortworx feature gate is disabled with an override.

### Am I vulnerable?

You may be vulnerable if all of the following are true:
- You are running a vulnerable version and have manually disabled the CSIMigrationPortworx feature gate.
- There are unprotected endpoints normally only visible from the control plane’s host network (including link-local metadata endpoints, unauthenticated services listening on localhost, or other services in the control plane’s private network).
- Untrusted users can create pods with the affected Portworx volume type.

#### Affected Versions

The CSIMigrationPortworx feature gate was enabled by default starting on version v1.31. As a result, EOL versions <= v1.30 are more likely to be vulnerable because the CSIMigrationPortworx feature is disabled by default.
- kube-controller-manager: <= v1.30.14
- kube-controller-manager: <= v1.31.14 
- kube-controller-manager: <= v1.32.9 
- kube-controller-manager: <= v1.33.5 
- kube-controller-manager: <= v1.34.1 


### How do I mitigate this vulnerability?

This issue can be mitigated by upgrading to a fixed kube-controller-manager version or by enabling the CSIMigrationPortworx feature gate (if it was overridden from its default value in versions greater than equal to v1.31).

#### Fixed Versions
- kube-controller-manager: >= v1.32.10
- kube-controller-manager: >= v1.33.6
- kube-controller-manager: >= v1.34.2

### Detection

This issue can be detected on clusters which have the CSIMigrationPortworx feature gate disabled on impacted versions by analyzing ProvisioningFailed events from kube-controller-manager which may contain sensitive information from the control plane’s host network.

If you find evidence that this vulnerability has been exploited, please contact [security@kubernetes.io](mailto:security@kubernetes.io)

#### Acknowledgements
This vulnerability was reported by:
- Xingyu Liu (xingyu@stu.xidian.edu.cn)
-  Jinku Li (jkli@xidian.edu.cn)

The issue was fixed and coordinated by:
- Ankit Gohil @gohilankit

comments.author: yliaog
comments.body:

title: ValidatingAdmissionPolicy namespace lookup raced newly created namespaces, produces spurious "namespace not found" rejections
security_topic: namespace lookup fallback missing in ValidatingAdmissionPolicy
qa_summary: Whether the namespace-lookup race in ValidatingAdmissionPolicy could wrongly reject requests, and the maintainer points to the fix in Kubernetes PR 135359.

comments.author: konryd
comments.body:
### What happened?

When creating new workload (observed with Deployment and StatefulSet) immediately after creating its namespace, there is a possibility that watch case has not yet caught up to the new namespace existing.

Naively, this would result in frequent failures, but apiserver guards against this by falling back to live client when namespace was `NotFound`. Example: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/ab3e83f73424a18f298a0050440af92d2d7c4720/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/admission/plugin/webhook/predicates/namespace/matcher.go#L88

The issue happens infrequently but can be forced by overriding informer lister to always return NotFound for a specific namespace (see repro instructions below). This way, the call to informer's lister would always fail, while the call to client would remain unaffected - this would force the fallback path, ensuring it is present.

### What did you expect to happen?

No 404 errors when creating StatefulSets in existing namespaces - even immediately after ns creation.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?



```
--- a/staging/src/k8s.io/client-go/listers/core/v1/namespace.go
+++ b/staging/src/k8s.io/client-go/listers/core/v1/namespace.go
@@ -20,7 +20,6 @@ package v1

 import (
        corev1 "k8s.io/api/core/v1"
-       errors "k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/api/errors"
        labels "k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/labels"
        listers "k8s.io/client-go/listers"
        cache "k8s.io/client-go/tools/cache"
@@ -47,17 +46,3 @@ type namespaceLister struct {
 func NewNamespaceLister(indexer cache.Indexer) NamespaceLister {
        return &namespaceLister{listers.New[*corev1.Namespace](indexer, corev1.Resource("namespace"))}
 }
-
-// Get retrieves the Namespace from the index for a given name.
-// Objects returned here must be treated as read-only.
-// This method overrides the embedded Get to add custom logic.
-func (nl *namespaceLister) Get(name string) (*corev1.Namespace, error) {
-       // 1. Check if the requested namespace is "lalala"
-       if name == "lalala" {
-               // 2. Return not found error if it is
-               return nil, errors.NewNotFound(corev1.Resource("namespace"), name)
-       }
-       // 3. Otherwise, use the parent implementation from the embedded ResourceIndexer
-       return nl.ResourceIndexer.Get(name)
-}
-
```


Steps to reproduce:

  2. Set up a cluster using that apiserver.
  3. Create the namespace "lalala"
  4. Create a StatefulSet in that namespace
  5. Observe the request failing with 404 - it should succeed despite the damaged lister code

### Anything else we need to know?

Based on our (limited) set of observations, we believe the regression happened between 1.32 and 1.33

Observations were made in GKE

N/A

title: [NodeDeclaredFeatures] GuaranteedQoSPodCPUResize version skew problem
security_topic: version-skew regression in node-declared features for pod CPU resize
qa_summary: Whether the NodeDeclaredFeatures change wrongly blocks previously allowed guaranteed pod CPU resizes, and the issue was resolved by removing the declared feature in Kubernetes PR 136759.

comments.author: tallclair
comments.body:
The `GuaranteedQoSPodCPUResize` node declared feature isn't just tied to the `InPlacePodVerticalScalingExclusiveCPUs` feature gate: it declares the feature if the feature gate is enabled OR the node doesn't use static CPU policy, and then requires the feature gate for all CPU resizes of guaranteed pods.

Here is the problem:
- v1.34 node: in-place pod resize is enabled, static policy disabled
	- 1.34 is pre-NDF, so it doesn't declare any features
- v1.35 control plane: NDF disabled (still alpha)
	- resizing guaranteed pod CPU is allowed (no NDF admission check), node doesn't mark resize as infeasible since it doesn't have static CPU policy.
- Upgrade cluster to v1.36: NDF goes beta & default enabled
	- Now resizing a guaranteed pod's CPU requires the `GuaranteedQoSPodCPUResize`, but the v1.34 node still doesn't set it, causing a regression.

I don't think we need to fix this in v1.35 since NDF is still alpha, but this is a beta-blocker.

/assign @pravk03 
/cc @natasha41575 
/milestone v1.36

comments.author: natasha41575
comments.body:
An idea I was toying around with when thinking about the other resize feasibility checks was inverting the logic: instead of the resize requiring a node declared feature to be set, the resize could be rejected if a feature is set.

In this case:
- Surface the node declared feature `InPlacePodVerticalScalingExclusiveCPUsDisabled` (or whatever name) if the node uses static CPU policy AND the feature gate is disabled
- During admission, *reject* the resize if the node declared feature `InPlacePodVerticalScalingExclusiveCPUsDisabled` is set

That way:
- ~with 1.36 control plane and 1.34 kubelet: the node declared feature will not be set, the patch will be permitted, and the 1.34 kubelet would run its feasibility checks (which would reject the resize as Infeasible)~
- with 1.36 control plane and 1.36 kubelet: the node declared feature *will* be set, and the patch will be rejected. 

Just my two cents!

ETA: Synced with Praveen offline, and have come to the understanding that ideally we would not rely on the kubelet checks in the old node, which makes sense.

comments.author: pravk03
comments.body: This is an issue with `GuaranteedQoSPodCPUResize` because it depends on both feature gate and node config and NDF is not GA. If the declared feature relied solely on the feature gate (like [InPlacePodLevelResourcesVerticalScaling](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/8d450ef773127374148abad4daaf28dac6cb2625/staging/src/k8s.io/component-helpers/nodedeclaredfeatures/features/inplacepodresize/pod_level_resource_resize.go)), this is not a problem.

comments.author: pravk03
comments.body:
> Surface the node declared feature InPlacePodVerticalScalingExclusiveCPUs (or whatever name) if the node uses static CPU policy AND the feature gate is disabled

I think we would still run into the same issue as `InPlacePodVerticalScalingExclusiveCPUs` feature graduates to Beta/GA.  I do not think its a good idea to have declared features based on inverse of feature gates.

comments.author: AadiDev005
comments.body:
It looks like the core challenge is the inconsistent behavior caused by the interplay of feature gates and node-declared features (NDF), especially across different Kubernetes versions.

One rough idea I’m considering is the concept of inverting the logic for the node declared feature: instead of requiring the feature to be set to allow resize, we reject the resize if an "exclusive CPUs disabled" feature is set on the node. This could help handle older nodes and avoid relying solely on kubelet checks in legacy versions.

I’d love to get feedback on this approach or any alternative ideas you think might make sense before digging deeper.

comments.author: tallclair
comments.body: @AadiDev005 was that an AI generated comment? It looks like you're just paraphrasing earlier comments and presenting the ideas as your own 😞

comments.author: tallclair
comments.body:
I think as it is, NodeDeclaredFeatures (NDF) doesn't match this use case. The problem stems from the fact that at the API level we're tightening the restrictions, by forbidding something that used to be allowed (resizing guaranteed pod CPU). This mostly stems from the fact that NDF didn't exist when we first introduced the feature gate for static CPU resize. If we had this feature gate from the beginning, it wouldn't have been an issue.

I think @natasha41575's suggestion to invert the logic, to have "Forbidden Features" rather than "Required Features" could be used for this, but I'm not sure we want to go that route. It's sort of weird for nodes to start advertising that they don't support a feature, since that implies that any node not advertising the negative feature DOES support it? Can we ever remove it in that case? Maybe this would be useful functionality to have for deprecations?

comments.author: pravk03
comments.body: Would it be acceptable to tighten the restrictions with NDF if there are existing Kubelet validations for the same feature ?. Specifically in the case of `GuaranteedQoSPodCPUResize`, the Kubelet currently marks resize requests with static policy as infeasible on nodes without NDF ([here](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/5bcb7599736327cd8c6d23e398002354a6e40f68/pkg/kubelet/allocation/allocation_manager.go#L693)), whereas on nodes with NDF, we reject the request during admission. While this admission behavior is inconsistent, it should resolve once NDF is enabled on all nodes. From the Pod's perspective, the net effect with and without NDF is the same ?

comments.author: tallclair
comments.body: Yeah, I think that's OK. In that case, we're just shifting the error to surface earlier. The problem we encountered in this issue is that pods that _wouldn't_ be marked infeasible can be rejected.

comments.author: natasha41575
comments.body:
> This mostly stems from the fact that NDF didn't exist when we first introduced the feature gate for static CPU resize.

I wonder if we should just state that NDF can't be used retroactively to block admission requests that would have previously succeeded. Net-new features (like PLR + IPPR) can make use of NDF if they are baked into the initial implementation/design, but otherwise it doesn't seem to fit the use case. 

This would make NDF useless for moving IPPR feasibility checks ... originally I was hoping it could be useful for `GuaranteedQoSPodCPUResize`, an analogous `GuaranteedQoSPodMemoryResize`, and maybe even resize + swap. But maybe not...

comments.author: pravk03
comments.body:
(Capturing discussions from slack and meetings)

The main concern here is that admission selectively depends on a feature gate, and NDF does not work well in such cases. 

Currently, `GuaranteedQoSPodCPUResize` is declared by the node when the below conditions are met 
- `InPlacePodVerticalScalingExclusiveCPUs` feature gate is enabled and Atatic CPU policy is enabled
**OR**
- Static CPU policy is disabled (feature gate is irrelevant here).

Since new declared features are not added on older nodes, requests that were previously allowed - specifically when the feature gate is irrelevant, would start to fail after the declared feature is added.

Based on the discussions, its better to stop declaring features that selectively depend on feature gates. I will make a change to stop declaring [GuaranteedQoSPodCPUResize](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/1861c1a07244e8e9430aaf588722dd22287c471e/staging/src/k8s.io/component-helpers/nodedeclaredfeatures/features/inplacepodresize/guaranteed_cpu_resize.go)

comments.author: SergeyKanzhelev
comments.body:
> Based on the discussions, its better to stop declaring features that selectively depend on feature gates. I will make a change to stop declaring [GuaranteedQoSPodCPUResize](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/1861c1a07244e8e9430aaf588722dd22287c471e/staging/src/k8s.io/component-helpers/nodedeclaredfeatures/features/inplacepodresize/guaranteed_cpu_resize.go)

what kind of feedback does this gives us? What would be the "correct" way of using NDF in cases like this going forward?

comments.author: natasha41575
comments.body:
> > Based on the discussions, its better to stop declaring features that selectively depend on feature gates. I will make a change to stop declaring [GuaranteedQoSPodCPUResize](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/1861c1a07244e8e9430aaf588722dd22287c471e/staging/src/k8s.io/component-helpers/nodedeclaredfeatures/features/inplacepodresize/guaranteed_cpu_resize.go)
> 
> what kind of feedback does this gives us? What would be the "correct" way of using NDF in cases like this going forward?

If there is a net-new feature, I think NDF can be used for these cases. The problem is that IPPR was implemented pre-NDF.

Say we had NDF at the time that IPPR was being implemented and we had used it. Version N control plane would selectively block admission requests where `GuaranteedQoSPodCPUResize` FG was not present. This is okay, because N-3 nodes would not have permitted IPPR at all, because it was not a supported feature. 

The problem is that we are trying to introduce NDF _after_ IPPR is GA. Version N control plane is blocking admission requests where `GuaranteedQoSPodCPUResize` FG is not present. But this is _not_ okay, because N-3 nodes do support IPPR, and we do not want control plane to block the request in all cases. 

For these cases, I think it just means that we have to wait for NDF to be GA+3.

comments.author: SergeyKanzhelev
comments.body:
> The problem is that we are trying to introduce NDF _after_ IPPR is GA. Version N control plane is blocking admission requests where `GuaranteedQoSPodCPUResize` FG is not present. But this is _not_ okay, because N-3 nodes do support IPPR, and we do not want control plane to block the request in all cases.

wouldn't this be a problem for any feature that went to beta, but then we discovered a blocker that needs to be restricting certain nodes from using the feature? Will the approach of two NDFs instead of one (Feature enabled, but feature is not working on this type of nodes) be preferable?

comments.author: natasha41575
comments.body:
> wouldn't this be a problem for any feature that went to beta, but then we discovered a blocker that needs to be restricting certain nodes from using the feature?

Yeah exactly, NDF is only useful for this case if we know what the restrictions need to be at the start. This is what I was trying to get across in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/135329#issuecomment-3752011625

comments.author: pravk03
comments.body:
> If there is a net-new feature, I think NDF can be used for these cases. The problem is that IPPR was implemented pre-NDF.

@natasha41575 I think we would have a problem with `InPlacePodVerticalScalingExclusiveCPUs` feature gate even if it were introduced as a declared feature after NDF was GA. The problem here is that `InPlacePodVerticalScalingExclusiveCPUs` is selectively used to determine if guaranteed QOS pod can be resized. A guaranteed pod resize on an older node with static CPU policy disabled would be incorrectly blocked.

comments.author: natasha41575
comments.body:
> > If there is a net-new feature, I think NDF can be used for these cases. The problem is that IPPR was implemented pre-NDF.
> 
> [@natasha41575](https://github.com/natasha41575) I think we would have a problem with `InPlacePodVerticalScalingExclusiveCPUs` feature gate even if it were introduced as a declared feature after NDF was GA. The problem here is that `InPlacePodVerticalScalingExclusiveCPUs` is selectively used to determine if guaranteed QOS pod can be resized. A guaranteed pod resize on an older node with static CPU policy disabled would be incorrectly blocked.

Ah I meant if NDF existed when IPPR itself was in alpha and we used it in this case all the way back then. In which case older nodes wouldn't have supported IPPR at all. But I think @SergeyKanzhelev's point is it will be impossible to always know in advance, during the development of alpha features, all the cases where we might need this.

comments.author: SergeyKanzhelev
comments.body: so would the better fix be to add two variables instead of one? One saying that `GuaranteedQoSPodCPUResize` present, another is saying `GuaranteedQoSPodCPUResizeBUT_THE_NODE_IS_STATIC` - disabling the resize

comments.author: natasha41575
comments.body:
> so would the better fix be to add two variables instead of one? One saying that `GuaranteedQoSPodCPUResize` present, another is saying `GuaranteedQoSPodCPUResizeBUT_THE_NODE_IS_STATIC` - disabling the resize

I'm struggling to understand how we would implement this without running into the same problem

comments.author: SergeyKanzhelev
comments.body:
> > so would the better fix be to add two variables instead of one? One saying that `GuaranteedQoSPodCPUResize` present, another is saying `GuaranteedQoSPodCPUResizeBUT_THE_NODE_IS_STATIC` - disabling the resize
> 
> I'm struggling to understand how we would implement this without running into the same problem

If neither defined - use older logic (allow if a bigger FG enabled). In this case - always allow.

If only `GuaranteedQoSPodCPUResize` defined in NDF - still allow. If both defined - disallow.

In future the resize will be imlpemeneted and both will be dropped to allow this again.

comments.author: pravk03
comments.body:
I am finding it a little hard to follow the suggestion. 

> If both defined - disallow.

If `InPlacePodVerticalScalingExclusiveCPUs` is true AND node has static policy , we should be allowing ?.  
We would still have the problem that an older node is not declaring anything but guaranteed QOS pod can be resized because node does not have static policy ?

comments.author: SergeyKanzhelev
comments.body:
> The core problem here is that the FeatureGate is irrelevant in some configs (static CPU policy disabled in this case) and we cannot use NDF in such cases.

this is why it might need two flags - one saying that there is a logic in kubelet that conditionally allow and disallow things and another - whether CPU static policy is enabled or not. Then the "neither" flags signal becomes consistent between older nodes and future nodes.

comments.author: natasha41575
comments.body:
Oh, I think I understand the suggestion. Let me try to paraphrase my understanding:

- Use `GuaranteedQoSPodCPUResizeBUT_THE_NODE_IS_STATIC` essentially as a signal about whether or not the kubelet has NDF for this feature 
- We block admission when `GuaranteedQoSPodCPUResize` is present, only if `GuaranteedQoSPodCPUResizeBUT_THE_NODE_IS_STATIC` is _also_ present. 

So N-3 nodes won't declare `GuaranteedQoSPodCPUResizeBUT_THE_NODE_IS_STATIC`, which would stop admission from erroneously blocking the resize.

This seems like a much better flavor of the reverse logic I suggested above, except in this solution we actually still have a means of removing the NDF in the future, when the static cpu resize feature is GA. 

ETA: Maybe I mixed up which flag to use for what but hopefully point still stands

comments.body: So, fundamentally we need to change the admission controller from "block by default and admit if declared feature/s present" to "admit by default and block if declared feature/s present". Currently, in scheduler and admission controller, NDF is used as an allow signal. The idea of using NDF to allow some features while denying others could be confusing ?

comments.body:
